newsitem.title: MEXICO: Opposition leads in poll for Mexico City vote.
newsitem.headline: Opposition leads in poll for Mexico City vote.

text.p: Mexico's left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) would win a slim victory in a crucial and historic race for mayor of Mexico City if elections were held now, a newspaper poll said on Wednesday.

In a poll of 798 voters carried out by Mexico City's Reforma newspaper 29 percent supported the PRD, 27 percent the conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN), 23 percent the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) and five percent the Mexican Green Ecology Party. Sixteen percent were undecided.
Reforma said its poll was carried out March 20-25. It gave no margin of error.
Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, the PRD candidate for the first ever mayoral election in Mexico City, is a two-time, former presidential candidate and son of a beloved former president.
The poll said the PAN, which has been ahead in voting preferences for Mexico City during most of last year, had fallen to second place after choosing lawyer Carlos Castillo Peraza as its candidate.
The July 6 vote will mark the first time residents of the capital directly elect their own leader. Mexican presidents have previously handpicked the Mexico City mayor.

Control of the lower house of Congress is also up for grabs in the mid-term July vote alongside several state governorships, making the elections the most voluable test of support for the long-ruling PRI.
Mexico's PRI has held almost total power in Mexico for 68 years. It has never lost presidency, and has always held all but a handful of governorships and a few local legislatures.
